stories.title: Langfuse groups batch-evaluation traces and scores by run
stories.summary: Langfuse 4.70.0 adds a shared batch identifier to evaluation outputs and a preview-gated tool for agents to start batch evaluations.
body: Langfuse records AI application activity and scores it with evaluators, which are saved checks of output quality or behavior. When engineers run those checks over many existing records, they need to distinguish that batch’s results from other evaluations. Version 4.70.0 adds batch_action_id metadata to each execution trace and score produced by a batch run. A trace records the work performed during an execution; the shared identifier lets operators find one batch’s outputs together.

For illustration, a team could rerun a revised answer-quality check over yesterday’s assistant responses. Grouping the resulting scores and evaluation traces by batch would help reviewers inspect that particular rerun. The identifier establishes which run produced a record; it does not establish that the evaluator’s judgement is correct.

The release also adds runBatchEvaluation through Model Context Protocol, an interface that lets agents call tools. The linked implementation limits tool availability to deployments with the preview opt-in enabled, requires evaluation permissions, and applies the plan’s data-access window. Langfuse’s in-app agent asks for approval before this tool runs. These are implementation conditions, rather than a claim that every deployment exposes the feature.
stories.takeaway: For Langfuse evaluation owners: verify a small batch’s traces and scores share its identifier, and check preview availability, permissions and the accessible date range before automating reruns.

stories.title: Phoenix fixes template-format and client-setting overrides in evaluations
stories.summary: Phoenix Evals 3.9.4 makes copied prompt templates use the requested format and lets client-specific settings override shared settings as documented.
body: Phoenix Evals is a library for checking AI outputs, including checks that ask a language model to judge an answer. Its 3.9.4 release fixes two cases where evaluation configuration did not behave as documented: changing the format of a copied prompt template, and giving a model client a setting that also appears in shared configuration.

A prompt template contains text with placeholders that are filled before the model sees it. Previously, copying a template with a different format changed its format attribute but retained the original parsing and rendering state. The fix rebuilds the template from its raw text when an override is supplied. For illustration, the regression test copies an f-string template containing {name} into Mustache format. That single-brace text should remain literal under the new format, rather than substitute a name.

The second fix merges shared and client-specific arguments before constructing synchronous or asynchronous clients. A shared timeout of 30 seconds and a synchronous override of 60 previously caused a duplicate-key error; the specific value now wins. The release’s linked changes include regression tests for both behaviors. These fixes concern evaluation setup and prompt rendering; they provide no evidence of improved judge accuracy.
stories.takeaway: For Phoenix Evals users who copy templates or customize client options: check rendered prompts and effective timeout values when upgrading, then rerun the affected evaluations.
